result:
The fix is in and PR #409 is marked ready: `arms.sh` now counts only a PR's own predictions toward its label, not everything ever collected from a branch with the same name. The PR is mergeable. CI on the pushed head (`a8ec8178b1`) had not been checked yet when I stopped, and the fold job waits on it.

**The rule** (in `label_decide()`, `docs/testing/jobs/arms.sh`): a verdict no longer counts toward a PR, and is no longer listed `withdrawn` on it, when its prediction file is already on master and the PR's diff against master doesn't touch it. That verdict belongs to an earlier PR that has already merged.

I used this instead of the brief's stricter "only predictions in the PR's diff" version. Under the strict version, a lane could clear a live `regressed` label just by deleting its own failed prediction file. The selftest includes a variant of the script with the strict version, and it fails on that case. Single-use `lane/<x>` branches behave exactly as before, and anything git can't answer keeps the old behaviour. The added cost is one `git diff` and one `git ls-tree` per label decision, so the tick doesn't get quadratic.

**#389 replay** (read-only against the live arms directory, nothing posted; full output in `docs/lanes/armsscope/NOTES.md`):

| | label | counted | listed withdrawn |
|---|---|---|---|
| before | `verified` | #60 texture-cache PASS | the four 09-20 GL FAILs |
| after | `none` | nothing | nothing |

**Tests:**
- The new `selftest.d/94-arms-verdict-scope.sh` covers all four cases in the brief, plus two more: a PR that edits an already-merged prediction still counts it, and deleting your own failed prediction keeps the FAIL.
- It also checks that a full tick posts nothing on the reused branch's PR, and it has three broken variants of the script, each of which fails the case it targets.
- The full selftest passed (1815 passed, 0 failed), but I ran it before merging master in. That merge brought in #408's new board-push-gate selftest fragment, so on the final head only preflight has passed; CI will run the selftest there.

**Not fixed here** (recorded in NOTES):
- If a reused branch's earlier PR was closed without merging, its predictions never reach master, so they still count toward the next PR on that branch. Fixing that means the strict rule and its deletion loophole. It hasn't happened in practice, because lane.remote's PRs get merged.
- For branches not named `lane/*`, `withdrawn_refs_for()` uses `origin/<branch>` before `pr/<n>`. The tick doesn't fetch `origin/<branch>` for those branches, so that ref can be out of date.
- The comment with a newly judged verdict still goes to whichever PR holds the branch at that moment. The brief only asked to scope the label.

There is no prediction or device arm, because nothing under `hw/` changed.
